overview: Thistle is a teacup-sized, nine-hundred-year-old fairy queen who makes bargains the way others breathe and never says thank you. Her route is about love that isn't a transaction, so the winning move is refusing to turn affection into a price.
tips: Her favourite gift is Moonflower Nectar; she also likes a Bouquet of Roses, Honey Cakes, a Gilded Hand Mirror, a Sparkling Gemstone, Exotic Perfume and a Cute Plushie. Avoid an Ordinary Fork, a Great Battle Axe and Clockwork Gears (she sneezes at iron).
Take her for a stroll through the Moonlit Gardens, her favourite date.
Her stat is Wits; Romance Scene II offers a Wits 3 counter-offer, though you can reach the same flag by simply refusing to sign her bargain.
Scene II is the fork: coaxing out her true name leads to Consort Under the Hill, while refusing her bargain leads to The Queen Who Set Down Her Crown.

endings.title: No Debts Between Us
endings.summary: Thistle keeps her crown, her court and her temper, and loves you with no contract and no price, running a lifelong ledger that never balances on purpose. It is the default ending, where she stays queen rather than taking you under the hill or abdicating.
howTo: This is the default ending, reached when you haven't set up either variant (or whenever you pick its final option).
At the festival, choose "We'll make it up as we go. No debts between us."

endings.title: Consort Under the Hill
endings.summary: You follow Thistle into the timeless Seelie palace beneath the hill to become her consort, where a night can be a year. Unlike the main ending, you leave the mortal world for fairyland rather than keeping her in Clicheton.
howTo: In Romance Scene II, when she offers her true name, choose "Tell me. I'll keep it safe."
At the festival, choose "Take me under the hill. Make me your consort."

endings.title: The Queen Who Set Down Her Crown
endings.summary: Thistle gives up her crown and nine centuries of rule to live a full-sized mortal life with you in town, iron and sneezes and all. This ending frees her from the throne entirely, the opposite of taking you into her court.
howTo: In Romance Scene II, refuse her bargain: either "No. I won't sign it." or the Wits 3 counter-offer "I'll love you, and you give me nothing. Write that in." (either outcome of the check works).
At the festival, choose "What if you didn't have to go back to the Court at all?"
